title: Cost Ledger Entry v1.0
description: Shape of ONE line of the GLOBAL (portfolio-wide) shared/cost_ledger.jsonl — the append-only, hash-chained reserve/confirm/release cost & quota ledger Faz-4 uses so 3-5 parallel project runs never blow a real budget (GSC daily call quota, DataForSEO credit pool, image-generation spend). The recorder (scripts/state/cost_ledger.py, AMO batch 4a) RESERVEs an estimate before costly work (refused with CostCeilingExceeded if it would exceed the operator ceiling), then CONFIRMs the actual (<= reserved) or RELEASEs (actual 0) after. USAGE(resource, period) = sum over reservation_ids of each reservation's EFFECTIVE amount (confirmed -> the actual; released -> 0; still-open -> the reserved amount), computed by replaying the INTACT chain. Hash-chained like consent.schema.json: entry_hash = sha256(canonical_json(this entry WITHOUT entry_hash)); prev_hash = the prior line's entry_hash (or 64 zeros for the genesis line) — a forged, rewritten, or reordered entry breaks the chain and verify_chain rejects it, so usage() fails CLOSED over tampered data. This is an append-only LOG (events.jsonl discipline; rules/append-only-state.md), NEVER an os.replace marker. The reservation_id is derived deterministically from the under-lock seq (e.g. 'r' + seq), so no clock/RNG is needed.

schema_version.description: ADR-018/019 const discipline; lets a future migration discriminate older entries.

seq.description: 0-based monotonic index of this entry within the file. seq 0 is the genesis line (prev_hash = 64 zeros). verify_chain asserts seq increments by exactly 1. The reservation_id of a reserve is derived from this seq.

op.description: reserve = hold an estimate against the ceiling (mints reservation_id 'r'+seq); confirm = record the ACTUAL spend (amount <= the reservation's reserved amount) for an open reservation; release = free an open reservation (amount 0). A reservation has at most one reserve then optionally one confirm OR one release (no double-free).

resource.description: The portfolio cost pool this entry charges. gsc_calls=Google Search Console daily call quota; dfs_credits=DataForSEO credit pool; image_spend=image-generation spend. confirm/release carry the SAME resource as the reservation they target so replay needs no back-reference lookup.

period.description: OPAQUE partition key passed in by the caller (clock-free): a daily pool passes the UTC date string ('2026-06-08'), a fixed quota passes a constant ('total'). USAGE filters entries by (resource, period); a new period is a fresh pool (daily-reset semantics). The module NEVER computes the date itself.

amount.description: For reserve: the estimate held against the ceiling. For confirm: the ACTUAL spend (<= the reservation's reserved amount). For release: 0. gsc_calls are integer counts; dfs_credits / image_spend may be fractional, so this is a number (>= 0).

reservation_id.description: Identifies the reservation. A reserve MINTS it deterministically from its under-lock seq ('r'+seq) — unique without a clock/RNG. A confirm/release carries the reservation_id it targets, so replay attributes the effective amount to the right reservation.

run_id.description: The run (or manual token) that wrote this entry — provenance for the audit trail. Usually a workflow run_id {slug}-{YYYY-MM-DD}-{hash4}; PERMISSIVE (minLength 1) to allow a standalone manual entry.

project_id.description: Slug of the project whose run charged this cost — provenance only (the ledger is portfolio-wide, keyed by resource+period, NOT by project). Matches project-config.schema.json's slug grammar.

recorded_at.description: UTC ISO 8601 when this entry was recorded. Passed in by the caller (the module is clock-free).

note.description: Optional free-text note (e.g. why a reservation was released).

prev_hash.description: entry_hash of the PRIOR line, or 64 zeros ('0'*64) for the genesis line (seq 0). The chain link.

entry_hash.description: sha256 hex over canonical_json of THIS entry with entry_hash removed (all other fields, incl. prev_hash, present). Tamper-evidence: recomputing must reproduce this value; usage() fails closed if any entry's hash does not reproduce.
